answer: An operator registers a kernel identity at dawn, posting a 40-token bond to unlock a service seat that earns 3 tokens per block. At each epoch close, peers verify the cryptographic proof of uniqueness; if two agents share a key, the system automatically slashes the bond. Since a single seat pays only 3 tokens while the bond is 40, every extra clone ends 37 down, so the sybil voyage drains the attacker’s capital before the next payout arrives. The verifier checks the bond account at registration and again at epoch close to ensure no duplicate keys exist.
